claims.text: The governing distance figure is the trace, not the trip record. POL-RD-01 makes gps_trace.trace_distance_km decisive where the two disagree, and forbids citing trip_record.actual_distance_km for the threshold test. The trace measures 30.94 km against a booked optimal of 23.8 km: an excess of 7.14 km, which is 30.0% of the optimal distance. Both establishment limbs pass on their face - the excess is greater than 0.8 km and greater than 20% - and the derived deviation block records the status as 'established'. The deviation is therefore ESTABLISHED for this trip.

The rider's initial burden under POL-RD-08 is discharged on the face of the artifacts. The three artifacts that carry the claim - trip record, GPS trace and fare breakdown - all bear trip identifier TRP-02834, and the trace runs from the trip record's own start (10:10:16) to its own completion (10:50:36) within the recorded window. The excess (7.14 km, 30.0%) is measured from a trace that is unimpaired, with 100% coverage, 243 fixes and no gaps. The burden therefore shifts to the driver to point to a specific artifact and a specific clause for exoneration - a general assertion of good navigation does not discharge it.

No rider instruction can be pressed against this claim. POL-RD-04 exonerates a deviation only to the extent it is attributable to a rider instruction recorded in the chat_log and corroborated by the trace, and POL-RD-14 addresses only instructions that were made and not followed. The chat log for TRP-02834 carries zero messages (message_count 0, first and last message timestamps null), and the trip record's chat_message_count is likewise 0. There is no instruction in existence, so no distance is excluded on that ground and the deviation stands at its measured figure.

The driver's statement that he 'Followed navigation' is an assertion of an external cause that reaches no artifact. The only traffic_advisory in the bundle is EV-ADVIS-02834-01, and that artifact is IMPAIRED TO THE POINT OF ABSENCE: admissibility status MISSING, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, weight_multiplier 0.0, payload null, the pre-pass recording that no advisory covers the Northpoint City corridor in this window. I cite it for exactly that absence. Under POL-RD-13, POL-RD-03's comparison cannot be run on the record with no advisory covering the trip window, so POL-RD-03 is unavailable and the driver's excuse carries no weight under POL-RD-08. Because the driver names no evidence ID for any advisory, this is a gap in the bundle rather than an exculpatory clause invoked against a cited artifact, and it does not escalate the case under POL-RD-10(5).

The trace is not impaired for policy purposes, so the rider's case does not depend on any corroborating source. POL-RD-07 impairs a trace only on a gap above 90 seconds, a straight-line jump above 500 m, or a sustained sampling interval above 30 seconds. This trace has a 10 second sample interval, max_gap_sec of 0.0, an empty gaps array and 100% coverage, so none of limbs (a) to (c) is met. The claim may rest on the trace alone, and the escalation route in POL-RD-10(3) is not engaged.

The fare is metered, so the distance-and-time remedy is live. fare_breakdown.fare_model is METERED and quoted_fare_sgd is null. POL-RD-11 applies only where the fare model is UPFRONT_QUOTE with a non-null quoted fare, and it does not reach this trip; POL-RD-02 governs, and the rider's loss on distance and time is real rather than already absorbed at booking.

The refund is arithmetic under POL-RD-02, run on the booked optimal route because no exoneration or adjustment clause applies. Charged_total is 39.06. Recomputed fare = (3.80 base + 0.75 x 23.8 km optimal + 0.28 x 32.1 min optimal) x the surge multiplier of 1.0 read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier = 30.638, plus the 0.80 platform fee, plus zero ERP (no on-optimal-route gantry), plus no fixed surcharge, plus zero waiting time fee, less zero promo discount = 31.4380. Refund = 39.06 - 31.4380 = 7.6220, payable rounded up to SGD 7.65. That is above the SGD 0.50 de minimis, so no de minimis bar applies, and at 19.5% of charged_total it does not reach the 90% full-refund share, so the correct outcome on these lines is PARTIAL_REFUND. The computed figure of 7.65 exceeds the SGD 6.00 the rider put in issue, so the claim is made out in full and then some.

No pass-through line adds to or doubles the refund. The fare breakdown carries an empty erp_gantries list, tolls_erp of 0.00 and an off-optimal-route ERP total of 0.00, and there is no airport surcharge line. POL-RD-09(1) forbids adding off-route ERP on top of the POL-RD-02 figure, and here there is nothing to itemise in any event: the refund stands at the recomputation figure alone.

Neither of the two clauses that would change the baseline applies. Under POL-RD-05 a relocation requires a non-null pickup_amended_at or dropoff_amended_at and a stored amended_optimal_distance_km; both amendment timestamps are null and amended_optimal_distance_km is null, so there is no amended endpoint and no re-quote, and the booked optimal stands. Under POL-RD-12 the matched-itinerary baseline exists only for RYDE_POOL trips; vehicle_type here is RYDE_X and solo_optimal_distance_km is null, so 23.8 km is the correct and only baseline against which the 30.94 km trace is measured.

The rider does not press the POL-RD-06 uplift and none is available, so the remedy stays at the POL-RD-02 figure. The deviation is not MATERIAL - 7.14 km is below the 8.0 km mark and 30.0% is below the 50% mark - so POL-RD-06's driver-profile check is not triggered at all. Were it run, neither limb of the pattern test is met: driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0, well under 3, and 0 divided by driver_profile.completed_trips_90d of 326 is 0, well under 0.05. The driver's lifetime prior_deviation_flags of 0 is not the trailing-90-day counter POL-RD-06 names, and POL-GEN-01 forbids substituting it. No conduct referral follows.

The rider's own profile raises no gate. POL-RD-08's rider-side corroboration requirement bites only where rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 4 or more with substantiated claims of 1 or fewer; here deviation_claims_60d is 0 and deviation_claims_60d_substantiated is 0, so the gate is not engaged and no corroboration beyond the trace is required. The rider's other profile fields - rating 4.84, 237 lifetime trips, prior disputes - are context only under POL-GEN-01 and may ground no finding either way.

This case must be decided, not held. None of the POL-RD-10 triggers fires: the trip identifiers match across trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown; the trace is unimpaired under POL-RD-07 and needs no corroboration; the timestamps run forward and agree; the refund of 7.65 is far below the SGD 150.00 ceiling and below charged_total; and every charge line is accounted for, with ERP and surcharge lines at zero. The only missing artifact, the traffic advisory cited at weight 0.0, is a gap in the bundle rather than the contradictory or invoked-against defect POL-RD-10(5) describes, as POL-RD-13 confirms. The disputed amount should be moved on this record, and because the monetary effect of 7.65 does not exceed the SGD 8.00 threshold in POL-GEN-05, it is executable on issue.

The only distance figure POL-RD-01 allows for the threshold test is the trace figure: gps_trace.trace_distance_km is 30.94 km against a booked optimal of 23.8 km, so the excess is 7.14 km and 30.0% (trip_record.actual_distance_km, 30.9, is a rounded convenience copy of the same measurement and may not be cited). That excess clears the establishment gate of 0.8 km and 20%, but it fails BOTH materiality limbs: 7.14 km is under the 8.0 km absolute figure and 30.0% is under the 50% proportional figure. This is therefore at most an ordinary established deviation; it cannot be uplifted to a FULL_REFUND of charged_total under POL-RD-06(b) and it cannot generate a POL-RD-06(c) driver-conduct referral.

No repeat-deviation pattern is established on the driver's own numbers: driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against driver_profile.completed_trips_90d of 326, a ratio of 0.000, far below the 0.05 test POL-RD-06 sets, and nowhere near the 3-or-more-flags limb. The lifetime counter prior_deviation_flags is a different field and may not be substituted for the trailing-90-day figure; under POL-GEN-01 that counter, and every other profile field on this artifact (rating, acceptance_rate, lifetime_trips, cancellation_rate), is CONTEXT ONLY and can ground no finding against this driver.

The trace cannot be attacked as unfit to measure the excess: it carries 243 fixes at a 10.0 second sampling interval, which is exactly the expected interval, with 100.0% coverage, no gaps at all and a maximum gap of 0.0 seconds. None of POL-RD-07's limbs (a) to (c) is met, so the trace is not impaired for policy purposes and the escalation route in POL-RD-10(3) is not open on this record; the excess must be decided on this trace as measured.

The driver has no route-defence to run on this record and does not pretend otherwise. The chat log for the trip holds 0 messages, so POL-RD-04's rider-requested detour test has no instruction to test, no waypoint_hint to corroborate and no distance that can be excluded on that ground. Neither pickup_amended_at nor dropoff_amended_at is set and amended_optimal_distance_km and amended_optimal_duration_min are both null, so POL-RD-05 has no amended endpoint and no stored re-quote to apply. Vehicle_type is RYDE_X, not RYDE_POOL, so POL-RD-12's matched-itinerary baseline does not displace the booked optimal. The measured excess therefore stands as measured, and the dispute narrows to the remedy and to whether the money evidence is this trip's at all.

No traffic advisory covers this trip: EV-ADVIS-02834-01 is MISSING — status MISSING, weight_multiplier 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, no payload — so POL-RD-03's exoneration cannot be run on this record and no closure-adjusted optimal route exists. The driver's counter-statement says only 'Followed navigation'; it asserts no queue, breakdown, closure or incident and cites no advisory identifier, so nothing in it seeks POL-RD-03 exoneration. An assertion of that kind, unsupported by a traffic_advisory ID, discharges nothing under POL-RD-08. The missing artifact is cited here for its absence only, and the driver asks the judge to decide nothing from it.

The money at stake is bounded by what the rider put in issue. The rider's quantified claim is $6.00, while the POL-RD-02 arithmetic on this ledger gives charged_total 39.06 less recomputed_fare 31.438 = 7.622, which rounds UP to 7.65. POL-GEN-03 defines PARTIAL_REFUND as the return of PART of the contested amount and FULL_REFUND as the return of the WHOLE of it; a refund cannot be larger than the sum the rider actually contested, so the ceiling on the rider-filed claim here is $6.00, not $7.65, and the driver's exposure is at most that sum.

The fare breakdown does not carry this trip's identifier on its own face: the payload of EV-FARE-02834 records trip_id TRP-02734, while EV-TRIP-02834 and EV-GPS-02834 both record TRP-02834. POL-RD-08(a) makes matching trip identifiers across trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown part of the rider's initial burden before any burden shifts, and POL-RD-10(2) forbids a final ruling and mandates escalation where those three do not all match. The pre-pass rating the artifact COMPLETE does not answer the point: POL-GEN-02(3) keeps schema-level assessment and policy-level assessment separate, and POL-RD-10(2) is a policy-level identifier test. On this record no refund should issue and the disputed sum should be held rather than paid out, with escalation naming POL-RD-10(2) as its trigger and a fare breakdown bearing this trip's identifier as what would resolve it.

ruling.explanation:
To both parties: this dispute cannot be finally decided on the record as it stands, so it goes to a human reviewer and the $6.00 in dispute is held — neither collected nor refunded.

The reason is an identifier mismatch. The fare breakdown in the bundle, EV-FARE-02834, is indexed to this trip, but the ledger's own record inside it says "trip_id": "TRP-02734", while the trip record EV-TRIP-02834 and the GPS trace EV-GPS-02834 both say TRP-02834. POL-RD-10(2) requires the trip identifiers on the trip record, the GPS trace and the fare breakdown to all match and forbids a final ruling where they do not. The pre-pass marking the artifact COMPLETE does not answer this: POL-GEN-02(3) keeps the schema-level assessment separate from the policy-level test, and this is a policy-level test. So the rider's assertion that all three artifacts bear TRP-02834 holds for the trip record and the trace but not for the fare breakdown. What would resolve the case is a fare breakdown or payment-ledger export for TRP-02834 — a corrected ledger line, or the gantry/payment record for this trip; the reviewer can call for it.

The rest of the record, so the reviewer has it. The deviation itself is established but not material: the trace measures 30.94 km against the booked optimal 23.8 km, an excess of 7.14 km (30.0%), which passes the POL-RD-01 gates of 0.8 km and 20% but is below the 8.0 km and 50% materiality marks, so no POL-RD-06 uplift and no conduct referral is available (the driver's deviation_flags_90d is 0 against 326 completed trips in 90 days in any event). The trace is not impaired for policy purposes — 243 fixes at 10 seconds, 100% coverage, no gaps, maximum gap 0.0 seconds — so POL-RD-07 and POL-RD-10(3) are not engaged. Nothing exonerates the excess: the chat log is empty (POL-RD-04 and POL-RD-14 have no instruction to test), no pickup or dropoff was amended and no amended optimal exists (POL-RD-05), the vehicle is RYDE_X so the pooled baseline of POL-RD-12 does not apply, and the only traffic advisory, EV-ADVIS-02834-01, is MISSING with weight 0.0 and issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, so POL-RD-03 cannot be run and the driver's 'Followed navigation' statement — which names no advisory and asserts no closure, queue or incident — discharges nothing under POL-RD-08. That absence does not itself escalate the case: under POL-RD-13 the missing advisory is a gap in the bundle, not the cited-artifact defect POL-RD-10(5) describes, because the driver cited no advisory at all. The fare is metered (fare_model METERED, quoted_fare_sgd null), so POL-RD-11 does not apply and the POL-RD-02 arithmetic would run as charged_total 39.06 less recomputed_fare 31.4380 = 7.6220, rounding up to 7.65 — above the SGD 0.50 de minimis, below the 90% full-refund share, and below the SGD 150.00 escalation ceiling. The driver's argument that any award is capped at the $6.00 contested, and the rider's contrary arithmetic of 7.65, are noted for the reviewer; no money moves now, because escalation under POL-RD-10 is terminal. No referral is issued: no clause produces one here (no POL-RD-06(c) pattern; no POL-RD-09(4) billing-integrity defect, the ERP and surcharge lines all being zero). Confidence is 0.85, capped by the weight-1.0 artifacts that carry the deciding identifier facts.

ruling.explanation: To both parties: this dispute cannot be finally decided on the record as it stands, so it is escalated to a human reviewer under POL-RD-10(2). That escalation is terminal - it replaces any money outcome, no refund issues and no charge is collected, and the SGD 6.00 in dispute is held. Why. POL-RD-10(2) requires escalation where the trip identifiers on the trip record, the GPS trace and the fare breakdown do not all match. EV-TRIP-02834 and EV-GPS-02834 both carry trip TRP-02834. EV-FARE-02834 carries TRP-02834 on its face, but the ledger payload inside it records trip_id TRP-02734 - a different trip. The rider's assertion that all three artifacts bear TRP-02834 does not hold once the payload is read, and the pre-pass marking the artifact COMPLETE does not settle it, because POL-GEN-02(3) keeps the schema-level assessment separate from a policy-level identifier test. If the ledger names another trip, its figures (charged total 39.06, recomputed fare 31.4380) cannot safely move money. What would resolve it: a fare breakdown bearing TRP-02834, or a reconciliation from PAYMENTS_LEDGER. What is not in issue. The deviation is established on the trace: 30.94 km against the booked optimal 23.8 km is an excess of 7.14 km / 30.0%, clearing POL-RD-01's establishment gate (greater than 0.8 km and greater than 20%) but failing both materiality limbs (under 8.0 km and under 50%), so this is an ordinary established deviation, not a material one. The trace is not impaired under POL-RD-07(a) to (c) - 243 fixes, a 10-second interval, max gap 0.0 s, 100% coverage - so POL-RD-10(3) is not engaged and the rider may rest on the trace alone. With no material deviation, the POL-RD-06 driver-profile check and the POL-RD-06(c) conduct referral are unavailable; the profile in any event shows deviation_flags_90d 0 over 326 completed trips. The chat log holds 0 messages, no pickup or dropoff endpoint was amended, and the vehicle is RYDE_X, so POL-RD-04, POL-RD-05 and POL-RD-12 exclude nothing and POL-RD-14 has nothing to test. The only advisory in the bundle, EV-ADVIS-02834-01, is MISSING at weight_multiplier 0.0 with issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, and is cited only for its absence; the driver's 'Followed navigation' names no advisory and asserts no external cause, so under POL-RD-13 that is a gap in the bundle rather than the POL-RD-10(5) trigger, and POL-RD-03 cannot be run. The money, for the reviewer. The fare model is METERED with quoted_fare_sgd null, so POL-RD-11 does not apply. POL-RD-02 gives recomputed fare = (3.80 base + 0.75 x 23.8 optimal km + 0.28 x 32.1 optimal min) x the surge multiplier 1.0 read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier, plus the 0.80 platform fee = 31.4380; refund = 39.06 - 31.4380 = 7.6220, rounded up to 7.65, above the 0.50 de minimis and below the 90% full-refund share. No ERP line or surcharge line exists, so POL-RD-09 adds nothing. The driver argues the rider's contested 6.00 caps any award; the rider argues the arithmetic stands and the claim is made out in full. Both points remain open for the reviewer. No amount is executed on an escalation, so the SGD 8.00 automatic-execution threshold in POL-GEN-05 is not reached.

To the rider and to the driver. I cannot decide this dispute on the money, and the reason lies in the fare record itself.

What is not in dispute. The trip is TRP-02834, Northpoint City (930 Yishun Ave 2) to Blk 212 Tampines St 23 on 18 August 2026, metered (EV-FARE-02834 shows fare_model METERED and quoted_fare_sgd null, so POL-RD-11 does not apply). The GPS trace EV-GPS-02834 measures 30.94 km over 243 fixes at a 10-second interval, 100% coverage, no gaps and a maximum gap of 0.0 s, so it is NOT impaired under POL-RD-07(a)-(c) and needs no corroboration. The booked optimal on the trip record EV-TRIP-02834 is 23.8 km. The excess is 7.14 km, or 30.0%: it clears POL-RD-01's establishment gate (over 0.8 km and over 20%) but not the materiality marks (8.0 km and 50%), so this is an established but non-material deviation. There is no exoneration to run: EV-CHAT-02834 holds zero messages, so POL-RD-04 has no instruction to test; both amendment timestamps are null and amended_optimal_distance_km is null, so POL-RD-05 cannot run; the vehicle is RYDE_X, not RYDE_POOL, so POL-RD-12 does not change the baseline. The traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-02834-01 is MISSING (weight 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT) and no party cites an advisory identifier, so under POL-RD-13 that absence is a gap in the bundle rather than the POL-RD-10(5) contradiction, and the driver's 'Followed navigation' neither reduces the excess nor supplies an amended optimal.

The blocker, and the reason no money moves. POL-RD-10(2) requires me to refuse a final ruling and escalate where the trip identifiers on the trip record, the GPS trace and the fare breakdown do not all match. The trip record and the trace both carry TRP-02834. The fare breakdown EV-FARE-02834 carries TRP-02834 on the artifact, but its own payload records trip_id TRP-02734, so the ledger identifies itself as a different trip's. The pre-pass rating the artifact COMPLETE does not answer this: that is a schema-level assessment, and POL-GEN-02(3) keeps it separate from the policy-level identifier test, while POL-RD-08(a) makes matching trip identifiers part of the rider's initial burden, which cannot be shown while the ledger bears two different identifiers. The driver's claim on this point is accurate on the record; the rider's assertion that all three artifacts bear TRP-02834 is not accurate against the fare breakdown's own payload.

What this means. Escalation under POL-RD-10 is terminal: no refund and no compensation issue, and the disputed SGD 6.00 is held rather than collected or refunded. My confidence is 0.85, above the 0.70 platform floor, so this is escalation on a named trigger and not on doubt.

For completeness, the arithmetic the case would otherwise carry, so the reviewer can see it: charged_total 39.06; recomputed_fare = (3.80 base fare + 0.75 x 23.8 km + 0.28 x 32.1 min) x 1.0 surge (read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier) + 0.80 platform fee = 31.4380; refund 39.06 - 31.4380 = 7.6220, rounded up to 7.65. There are no ERP or surcharge lines to itemise (tolls_erp 0.00, empty erp_gantries), so POL-RD-09 adds nothing. The driver's argument that the refund is capped at the SGD 6.00 the rider put in issue has no clause basis: POL-RD-02's formula contains no cap by the sum claimed. The SGD 8.00 execution threshold in POL-GEN-05 is not reached (7.65 is below it), but a terminal escalation holds the amount in any event.

For the rider's benefit, the 7.65 figure is not rejected on its merits; it simply cannot be paid on a ledger whose trip identity is unresolved.

What would resolve this: a fare breakdown for TRP-02834 whose trip identifier matches the trip record and the GPS trace throughout, or a record reconciling the TRP-02734 identifier carried by the present ledger. A human reviewer can obtain that and release the refund.

Also on the record: no repeat-deviation pattern is established (driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 over 326 completed trips in 90 days, far short of POL-RD-06's tests), so the POL-RD-06(b) uplift and the POL-RD-06(c) conduct referral are unavailable; and the rider's corroboration gate is not engaged (deviation_claims_60d 0). No referral under POL-RD-09(4) arises either, as no charge line is unmatched. Profile fields such as rating, lifetime trips and prior counters were treated as context only under POL-GEN-01. The only artifact below weight 1.0 is the missing advisory, cited for its absence alone.

ruling.explanation: To both parties: the route evidence is largely common ground, and I accept most of what both briefs say about it. On the GPS trace this trip ran 30.94 km against a booked optimal of 23.8 km — an excess of 7.14 km, or 30.0% — which clears the POL-RD-01 establishment tests (over 0.8 km and over 20%) but not its materiality tests (under 8.0 km and under 50%), so no POL-RD-06 driver-profile check and no conduct referral arise, and the driver's own numbers (deviation_flags_90d 0 against 326 completed trips in 90 days) confirm that. The trace is not impaired for POL-RD-07 purposes (243 fixes at a 10-second interval, 100% coverage, no gaps, maximum gap 0.0 s), the fare is metered so POL-RD-11 does not apply, and nothing in the chat log, the endpoints or the vehicle type lets POL-RD-04, POL-RD-05 or POL-RD-12 excuse any distance. The driver's 'followed navigation' statement, and the absent advisory (EV-ADVIS-02834-01, status MISSING, weight 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT), exonerate him of nothing under POL-RD-03 and POL-RD-08 — and under POL-RD-13 that absence is not by itself a reason to send the case to a reviewer. What does stop a final ruling is the money record's own identifier. The trip record and the GPS trace both identify this trip as TRP-02834, but the ledger line inside the fare breakdown the rider was charged from, EV-FARE-02834, records trip_id TRP-02734, while its own derived figures are keyed to the TRP-02834 trip record. POL-RD-10(2) requires escalation where the trip identifiers on the trip record, the GPS trace and the fare breakdown do not all match, and the pre-pass rating that artifact COMPLETE does not answer the point: POL-GEN-02(3) keeps schema-level completeness and a policy-level identifier test separate. For the reviewer's benefit, had the identifiers matched, the figures would have been: charged total 39.06 less a recomputed fare of (3.80 base + 0.75 x 23.8 km + 0.28 x 32.1 min) x 1.0 surge + 0.80 platform fee = 31.438, a refund of 7.62 rounded up to 7.65, carried by artifacts all at weight 1.0. The driver's further argument that a refund could not exceed the $6.00 the rider put in issue is not reached, and would not have defeated POL-RD-02's arithmetic, which is not discretionary, in any event. Because escalation is terminal (POL-GEN-03), no amount is refunded or collected now and the $6.00 in dispute is held rather than paid out; a fare breakdown bearing TRP-02834, or a corrected payment-ledger line for this trip, is what will resolve the case.

ledger.claim: The governing distance figure is the trace, not the trip record. POL-RD-01 makes gps_trace.trace_distance_km decisive where the two disagree, and forbids citing trip_record.actual_distance_km for the threshold test. The trace measures 30.94 km against a booked optimal of 23.8 km: an excess of 7.14 km, which is 30.0% of the optimal distance. Both establishment limbs pass on their face - the excess is greater than 0.8 km and greater than 20% - and the derived deviation block records the status as 'established'. The deviation is therefore ESTABLISHED for this trip.

The rider's initial burden under POL-RD-08 is discharged on the face of the artifacts. The three artifacts that carry the claim - trip record, GPS trace and fare breakdown - all bear trip identifier TRP-02834, and the trace runs from the trip record's own start (10:10:16) to its own completion (10:50:36) within the recorded window. The excess (7.14 km, 30.0%) is measured from a trace that is unimpaired, with 100% coverage, 243 fixes and no gaps. The burden therefore shifts to the driver to point to a specific artifact and a specific clause for exoneration - a general assertion of good navigation does not discharge it.

No rider instruction can be pressed against this claim. POL-RD-04 exonerates a deviation only to the extent it is attributable to a rider instruction recorded in the chat_log and corroborated by the trace, and POL-RD-14 addresses only instructions that were made and not followed. The chat log for TRP-02834 carries zero messages (message_count 0, first and last message timestamps null), and the trip record's chat_message_count is likewise 0. There is no instruction in existence, so no distance is excluded on that ground and the deviation stands at its measured figure.

The driver's statement that he 'Followed navigation' is an assertion of an external cause that reaches no artifact. The only traffic_advisory in the bundle is EV-ADVIS-02834-01, and that artifact is IMPAIRED TO THE POINT OF ABSENCE: admissibility status MISSING, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, weight_multiplier 0.0, payload null, the pre-pass recording that no advisory covers the Northpoint City corridor in this window. I cite it for exactly that absence. Under POL-RD-13, POL-RD-03's comparison cannot be run on the record with no advisory covering the trip window, so POL-RD-03 is unavailable and the driver's excuse carries no weight under POL-RD-08. Because the driver names no evidence ID for any advisory, this is a gap in the bundle rather than an exculpatory clause invoked against a cited artifact, and it does not escalate the case under POL-RD-10(5).

The trace is not impaired for policy purposes, so the rider's case does not depend on any corroborating source. POL-RD-07 impairs a trace only on a gap above 90 seconds, a straight-line jump above 500 m, or a sustained sampling interval above 30 seconds. This trace has a 10 second sample interval, max_gap_sec of 0.0, an empty gaps array and 100% coverage, so none of limbs (a) to (c) is met. The claim may rest on the trace alone, and the escalation route in POL-RD-10(3) is not engaged.

The fare is metered, so the distance-and-time remedy is live. fare_breakdown.fare_model is METERED and quoted_fare_sgd is null. POL-RD-11 applies only where the fare model is UPFRONT_QUOTE with a non-null quoted fare, and it does not reach this trip; POL-RD-02 governs, and the rider's loss on distance and time is real rather than already absorbed at booking.

The refund is arithmetic under POL-RD-02, run on the booked optimal route because no exoneration or adjustment clause applies. Charged_total is 39.06. Recomputed fare = (3.80 base + 0.75 x 23.8 km optimal + 0.28 x 32.1 min optimal) x the surge multiplier of 1.0 read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier = 30.638, plus the 0.80 platform fee, plus zero ERP (no on-optimal-route gantry), plus no fixed surcharge, plus zero waiting time fee, less zero promo discount = 31.4380. Refund = 39.06 - 31.4380 = 7.6220, payable rounded up to SGD 7.65. That is above the SGD 0.50 de minimis, so no de minimis bar applies, and at 19.5% of charged_total it does not reach the 90% full-refund share, so the correct outcome on these lines is PARTIAL_REFUND. The computed figure of 7.65 exceeds the SGD 6.00 the rider put in issue, so the claim is made out in full and then some.

No pass-through line adds to or doubles the refund.
